DOCUMENTS.note: Curated, deduplicated, ATOMIC document list (one real document per entry - never a combined/comma-joined value). Combinations are built by the user via the Mandatory + Any-one-of document-builder UI, never pre-baked into this list. 'Other' always available as free text for genuinely new document names. Cleaned 2026-08-18 (candidate-empathy audit): 'Highest Passing Education Marksheet or Degree' had its own 'or' baked into the label, which is now redundant and confusing since the Any-one-of picker is a first-class UI mechanism - split into its own atomic 'Highest Passing Education Marksheet' entry ('Degree' already existed separately, pick both into Any-one-of to reproduce the same either/or); 'Both-side colour copy of University-issued Degree' merged into plain 'Degree' since the both-side/colour-copy detail is already expressible via the Special Instructions checkboxes, not part of the document's identity; 'Graduation or above education documents' relabeled to 'Graduation (or higher) Education Documents' for clarity (the 'or' here describes an education LEVEL, not a choice between two named documents, so it was not split). SECOND CLEANUP PASS (2026-08-21, owner: 'clean the values, I see duplicates - what if Ops guy selects both, that will create a clumsy comment'): removed 3 values that were the same real document as one already in the list, just worded differently, so an agent could tick both and produce a redundant sentence - 'Degree certificate' merged into 'Degree' (same document); 'Original copies of University-issued Final year marksheet' merged into 'Final year marksheet' (the 'original'/'university-issued' qualifier belongs in Special Instructions - see 'Original document, not a photocopy' and 'Sealed and signed by the institution' there - not in the document's identity); 'Letter of Authorization' merged into 'Authorization form' (same document, both real phrasings - 'Authorization form' kept since it's the shorter, more checkbox-friendly label). NOT merged, despite looking similar, because real-data frequency shows they're genuinely distinct, separately-used documents (checked via grep across all 8,284 real comments): 'HEDD consent form' (50 real mentions) vs plain 'Consent form' (136 real mentions, excluding HEDD) - both used independently at real volume, not one rare variant of the other. STILL FLAGGED, not yet merged (owner judgment call needed - see PROGRESS_LOG.md 2026-08-21 entry): 'Highest Passing Education Marksheet' (3 real mentions) / 'Highest completed education documents' (24) / 'Graduation or Higher Education Documents' (60) may be 3 overlapping phrasings of the same ask, or may be genuinely different asks by education-level granularity - real-data volume alone can't settle which. THIRD CLEANUP PASS (2026-08-21, owner: 'where are sem 1-8 and all semester marksheet options? you are missing some educational docs and added some unnecessary values'): grepped all 8,284 real comments for 'semester' - confirmed 11 real rows explicitly ask for a specific numbered semester's marksheet ('Require 1st Semester Marksheet' through '...8th Semester Marksheet') or 'All Semester Marksheet' as its own request, distinct from year-wise marksheets (semester-run programs, e.g. most B.Tech/B.E. courses, don't have 'years' as a submission unit) - this whole category was completely absent before this pass; added 9 new atomic values below. Also removed 'Graduation or Higher Education Documents' - grepped for the literal document phrase and found ZERO real occurrences; the underlying idea ('graduation or above', 405 real mentions) is real and common, but it's a QUALIFICATION-LEVEL descriptor that belongs with COURSE_NAME context, not a distinct document - the actual documents those 405 real rows ask for are already covered by the existing 'Degree'/'Final year marksheet'/'All year marksheets' entries, so this value was pure duplication of those under a confusing, evidence-free label. FOURTH CLEANUP PASS (2026-08-26, from an external domain-expert review): 'Transcripts and Marksheets' violated the atomic-value rule (a bundled 'X and Y' string, same class of problem the DOCUMENTS_ATOMIC redesign exists to prevent). Checked all 11 real rows carrying this phrase (157 weighted occurrences) - 100% appear in the exact same fixed real sentence, 'Kindly provide Degree certificate, Transcripts and Marksheets of the candidate.', always alongside 'Degree' (already its own atomic value) - so the 'Marksheets' half is pure duplication of the existing 'All year marksheets'/'Final year marksheet' entries, and the 'Transcripts' half is a genuinely distinct real document (an official academic transcript, not the same artifact as a marksheet) with zero standalone real mentions to confirm an exact different atomic wording. Replaced 'Transcripts and Marksheets' with a new atomic value 'Academic Transcript' - an agent reproducing the historical combined ask now picks 'Degree' + 'Academic Transcript' + 'All year marksheets'/'Final year marksheet' as separate Mandatory-bucket picks, which is exactly what the document-builder mechanism is for. REVIEWED, KEPT AS-IS (2026-08-26, same external review): 'Highest completed education documents' and 'Second highest completed Education Documents' were flagged as meta-categories rather than atomic document names (correct observation - unlike 'Degree' or 'Final year marksheet', they don't name a specific document). Checked real-data weight before deciding: 1,205 weighted real rows use one of these two phrases with NO specific document named anywhere in the same comment (vs. only 3 weighted rows where a concrete document was also named alongside it) - this is among the highest real-usage weight of any value in this entire list, not a rare artifact, meaning real BGV agents genuinely and routinely ask this way without knowing/needing to specify which exact document. Owner decision (given this evidence): kept both values as-is rather than retiring them - removing them would break the tool's ability to reproduce ~1,200 real historical comments where the agent legitimately never named a specific document. Not merged with each other or with any atomic document value, since 'highest' vs 'second highest' is a real, load-bearing distinction (which of the candidate's qualifications is meant) that a specific document name can't express on its own. FIFTH CLEANUP PASS (2026-08-26, second batch from the same external review - 8 proposed values with scope/context/confidence columns): checked each against search_index.json before deciding, not accepted on the external reviewer's stated confidence alone. ADDED: 'Professional License' [D] - genuinely real and CURRENTLY MISSING despite being actively used: 16 real rows / 58 weighted occurrences ('...Clear and complete scanned Professional License with Roll/Registration Number', 'Kindly Provide document of Professional License'), already resolving to live templates T9/T13, but the bare document name had never been added to this atomic list - a real gap, not a speculative addition, found precisely because the external review prompted a fresh look. NOT ADDED, with reasoning: 'Convocation Certificate / Degree Award Scroll' - the reviewer's own framing describes this as the document issued when a degree is formally conferred, which is functionally the same real-world artifact as the existing 'Degree' value; adding it risked exactly the 'Ops guy ticks both, produces a redundant sentence' problem this list has been cleaned of twice already (see SECOND CLEANUP PASS), with no real evidence to justify treating it as a genuinely distinct document. 'Third-Party Verification Portal Consent Form' - checked 'WES'/'NSC'/'Qualification Check' as exact words (not substrings) against all 8,284 real comments and found ZERO real hits for any of the three (an initial substring search had false-positived on 'WES' inside 'West Bengal' and 'NSC' inside 'traNSCripts'); the underlying document concept is also already covered by the existing 'Authorization form'/'Consent form' values - if a specific portal (WES/NSC/etc.) does turn up in real data later, the right place for it is a new PORTAL_NAME value (which already lists HEDD/Parchment/etc.), not a new DOCUMENTS entry. SIXTH CLEANUP PASS (2026-08-26, seventh external review batch, proposed as a new standalone FEE_PAYMENT_STATUS tag): rather than create an orphan tag wired into no live template (the two document-type proposals in that batch aren't a 'status' at all - they're physical documents), redirected 2 of the 4 proposed values here as new atomic documents: 'Payment Proof / Bank Transaction Receipt' (zero direct real hits, Ops judgment) and 'Demand Draft / Pay Order' (1 real row/1 weighted - 'DD Proof' - supports this as a real, distinct document type, not covered by any existing value). The other 2 proposed values from that same batch were NOT added here: 'Verification fee payment required from candidate' is a STATUS/reason, not a document - already covered by the existing VERIFICATION_BLOCKER value 'Verification fee payment pending from the candidate'; 'Fee paid, awaiting university reconciliation' is also a status, not a document - added instead as a new VERIFICATION_BLOCKER value (see that tag's own note). 'Bonafide Certificate' as a value distinct from the existing 'Bonafide/NOC' - checked all 64 real rows containing 'bonafide' (186 weighted) and found ZERO that mention 'bonafide' without 'NOC' immediately alongside it - real usage never separates the two, so splitting them would create an unevidenced distinction. 'Official Academic Transcript in Sealed Envelope' - not added as a DOCUMENTS value at all; this describes a HANDLING requirement on top of the already-existing 'Academic Transcript' document, not a different document, so it was added instead as a new SPECIAL_INSTRUCTIONS value (see that tag's own note) restricted to 'Academic Transcript' via applies_to_documents, mirroring how 'Original document, not a photocopy' already works. RENAMED 2026-08-27 (task #115, owner): the atomic value 'Degree' is now 'Degree Certificate'. Same single value, clearer label - bare 'Degree' reads as the qualification level rather than the physical document, and every sibling here already names the artefact ('Provisional Certificate', 'Migration Certificate', 'Transfer Certificate'). This is the SAME merged entry the 2026-08-21 SECOND CLEANUP PASS created when it folded a then-separate 'Degree certificate' into 'Degree' - it only flips which of those two labels survives, and does NOT reintroduce the duplicate pair. Covers the Mandatory and Any-one-of buckets alike, since both render from this one list. INCOMPLETE_DETAIL.note: New tag for T73 ('Incomplete - Other Detail', added 2026-08-24, owner-approved Document Reason revamp: 'add more and standardise the values... each value should be reusable') - a reusable, document-type-agnostic checklist of what makes a submitted document incomplete, used alongside T11 (generic Incomplete), T53 (missing company details - kept as its own distinct scenario since it needs the company-name callout), and T66 (wrong format - kept distinct for the same reason). Multiselect since a real submission can genuinely be incomplete for more than one reason at once (e.g. both missing a signature AND missing a page). Not yet confirmed against real classified data - built on Ops common-sense per the owner's explicit request, stated plainly rather than presented as dataset-confirmed. EXPANDED 2026-08-26 (external review, 5 proposed values): checked each against search_index.json - all 5 came back essentially zero direct real evidence (one 'First Division' hit was a course-name/academic-distinction mention, not a flagged omission; a 'Digilocker' hit just referenced the portal, not a truncated seal), consistent with this tag's existing zero-dataset-confirmation status from when it was first built. Added 4 of the 5, all `[O]`, since they're structurally distinct from the existing 6 values and from each other, not near-duplicates: 'Missing Roll/Registration Number or Student ID on the document' (distinct from the IDENTIFIER_TYPE tag's own similar-sounding value - IDENTIFIER_TYPE/T15 is about the candidate never having GIVEN AuthBridge this number at all, this is about a SUBMITTED document's own printed content lacking it; given how overwhelmingly often real comments ask for a document 'with Roll/Registration Number' - 3,559 weighted rows - this is a highly plausible incomplete-document pattern even with no direct real hit for the omission itself), 'Missing grade scale / CGPA-to-percentage conversion formula', 'Missing Month/Year of Passing or Graduation Date on the document' (again distinct from ANTECEDENTS' similar 'Passing year' value, which is a case-level information-mismatch concept, not a document-content-completeness one), 'Missing division/class awarded (e.g. First Class, Distinction)'. NOT added here: 'Barcode/QR Code/Digital Verification Seal truncated or unreadable' - this describes a SCAN-QUALITY defect (something present but unreadable/cut off), which structurally belongs with BLUR_DETAIL's existing 'Image is cropped or cut off' concept, not with this tag's missing-content framing - added to BLUR_DETAIL instead (see that tag's own note) rather than force-fit here.

Multiselect for the same reason as INCOMPLETE_DETAIL above - a scan can be both faded AND cropped at once. Not yet confirmed against real classified data - built on Ops common-sense per the owner's explicit request, stated plainly rather than presented as dataset-confirmed. ADDED 2026-08-26 (external review, redirected from an INCOMPLETE_DETAIL proposal): 'Barcode/QR code/digital verification seal is truncated or unreadable' - zero direct real hits (a 'Digilocker' match found while checking was just a portal reference, not a truncated-seal report), but this describes a scan-quality defect on modern digital certificates (DigiLocker, e-transcripts), which is this tag's territory (a narrower, more specific case of the existing 'Image is cropped or cut off'), not INCOMPLETE_DETAIL's missing-content territory. FIFTH BATCH (2026-08-26, external review, 4 proposed values): zero real hits for any of the 4 (checked 'watermark', 'glare'/'reflection', 'pixelat'/'low-resolution', 'shadow'/'uneven lighting' against all 8,284 real comments), but all 4 describe genuinely distinct physical/optical scan defects not covered by the existing 5 values (watermark obscured, glare, digital pixelation, and shadow are each a different root cause than 'blurred'/'faded'/'cropped') - added `[O]`, same convention as this tag's original build.

A case can genuinely be missing more than one identifier at once (e.g. both Roll/Registration Number and a Hall Ticket No.) - no different in kind from ANTECEDENTS/CASE_LEVEL_INFORMATION/VERIFICATION_BLOCKER, all already multiselect for the same reason. UPDATED 2026-08-23 (owner asked 'have you checked with the actual comments?' re: the small Information-category value sets): re-ran extraction across ALL 8,284 rows (not just Information-template-matched ones) - found 22 distinct real IDENTIFIER_TYPE values total; the ~12 that looked 'not in dropdown' were almost all casing/punctuation variants of values already here ('exam Roll No', 'student ID number', 'Hall Ticket No.' etc. - same concept, different capitalization/period), not genuine gaps. DUPLICATE WARNING REVIEWED, NOT MERGED (2026-08-26, external review suggested consolidating 'Exam Roll No'/'Roll/Registration Number'/'Hall Ticket No' into standard identifiers): checked exact real-text volume for each independently - 'Roll/Registration Number' (3,551 rows/5,976 weighted), 'Hall Ticket No' (28 rows/33 weighted), 'Exam Roll No' (5 rows/23 weighted) - all three appear as their OWN distinct real phrasing across hundreds to thousands of real comments, not as case/punctuation variants of each other (unlike the earlier casing-variant cleanup this note already documents). Converted to multiselect 2026-08-18 (candidate-empathy audit) — a real rejection can have more than one simultaneous cause (e.g. both blurred AND signatures mismatched); safe to multiselect everywhere it's used because every template places it at the end of a "because X" clause, which reads correctly whether one or several reasons are AND-joined. VERIFICATION_BLOCKER.applies_to_templates_note_20260825: Added 2026-08-25 (owner: 'wherever it would look accurate and correct, there it should be' - re: T13/T63 showing the full 20-value list including reasons that don't fit a 'please provide an acceptable copy' resubmission ask). Root-caused via search_index.json's real extracted_tags, grouped by resolved_template_id: T13's real VERIFICATION_BLOCKER values (14 distinct, e.g. 'Documents not sufficient', 'Clear and complete scanned', 'both side colored copies required', 'mismatch found in the course name', 'not in Opencert file format') are ALL document-quality/mismatch defects a candidate can actually fix by resubmitting a better copy. T6's real values (11 distinct: 'Non Recognized Institute', 'Verification of this document has been disabled by the document owner', 'pending dues', 'records related to the certificate cannot be found', 'letterhead verification is not possible') are institutional/process blockers a document resubmission cannot fix at all - asking a candidate to 'provide an acceptable copy' because 'Dues are pending with the institute' doesn't logically follow, since a new copy of the same document does nothing to clear dues. Restricted these 5 values (absent-is-universal, same convention as ANTECEDENTS/DOCUMENTS/SPECIAL_INSTRUCTIONS) to T6 (Candidate Non-Cooperation/Verification blocked) and T60 (TAT extension request) only - both ask the CLIENT how to proceed rather than asking the candidate to fix a document, so any blocking reason (document-related or not) is valid context there. This is a real, common requirement for US/UK/Canada institutions specifically for official transcripts (registrars often refuse a scanned upload and require the document to arrive directly from the issuing institution) - zero real hits for this exact requirement in the current 8,284-row dataset, so added on Ops judgment (stated plainly, not dataset-confirmed), but it's a genuine HANDLING instruction on an existing document rather than a new document in its own right, so it belongs here rather than as a new DOCUMENTS entry (see that tag's note for the full reasoning on why it wasn't added there). FIFTH BATCH (2026-08-26, external review, 5 proposed values): checked each against real data and against the existing 10 values before acting. ADDED, all `[O]` (zero direct real hits for any of the 3): 'Downloaded directly from the issuing portal (e.g. DigiLocker/university portal) - not a photo/screenshot' (a distinct SOURCE-CHANNEL requirement, not a copy-quality one - 1 real row confirms DigiLocker is a real channel in this dataset, though not phrased as this exact instruction); 'Attested by a Gazetted Officer or Notary Public' (distinct from the existing 'Self-attested by the candidate' - THIRD-PARTY attestation is a different real requirement, common for Indian document submissions); 'Must be issued on official university/college letterhead' (a forward-looking submission instruction, distinct from VERIFICATION_BLOCKER's existing backward-looking 'Letterhead verification is not possible for this institute' rejection reason - 79 weighted real rows confirm letterhead is a live, common concern in this dataset, substantiating it as worth having on the instruction side too, not just the rejection side).
